newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond new issue trips on market fears. [CORRECTED 01:25 GMT 11/7]
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond new issue trips on market fears. [CORRECTED 01:25 GMT 11/7]

text.p: (Corrects headline to make clear that only one issue reacted to the market).

U.S. corporate bond new issue activity opened on a sour noted Thursday on news Iridium LLC was forced to reduce its mega-junk bond offering due to investor concerns about the risks involved in the deal, market sources said.
In the investment-grade sector, Philip Morris Cos Inc priced a $1 billion global debt offering at 79 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
Merrill Lynch & Co, the deal's underwriter, originally set price talk at 78 to 80 basis points (corrects from 76 to 79 basis points) over Treasuries.

Iridium was forced to drop a $250 million zero coupon tranche and increase to 13 percent the price talk on a $500 million tranche of cash-pay bonds (B3/B-), according to market sources. Price talk was originally 12 to 12-1/4 percent.
"This is a more cautious market environment and it comes as no surprise that aggressively priced offerings like Iridium's are struggling," said a syndicate official away from the deal.
He added, "People are just getting nervous about how long this great market is going to last."
Investors are worried about Iridium's ambitious plan to build a satellite-based global communications network.
Market sources said Philip Morris' was forced to pay investors a considerable risk premium in its global offering of eight-year debt (A2/A) due to the risks surrounding the tobacco settlement.
The bonds were trading at a spread of 77 to 79 basis points after the deal was priced, a trader said.
Elsewhere, SAFECO Corp was close to selling a large offering of capital securities and senior notes via Smith Barney Inc.
Price talk on the $750 million in 40-year capital securities is 147 to 150 basis points over Treasuries.
Sources said a $200 million senior note tranche is expected to be priced with a spread in the high 60-basis-point area.
In the high-yield new issue market, HMH Properties plans to sell $600 million in 10-year senior notes (Ba3/BB-) via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette on Thursday afternoon.
Price talk is 250 to 275 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Ameristar Casinos Inc is also expected to price $100 million in seven-year senior subordinated notes (B3/B-) via Bear Stearns & Co Inc on Thursday.
